panels.description: At-a-glance scrape health, synchronization, peers, and storage for both node processes.
panels.title: Overview

panels.description: OP Node unsafe L2 head minus the execution-layer canonical head. Zero means the execution client has caught up to the consensus head.
panels.title: EL Head Gap

panels.description: Unsafe-to-safe L2 backlog. This is normally non-zero because safe blocks depend on L1 batch derivation.
panels.title: OP Safe Lag

panels.description: World Chain's separate Flashblocks protocol peer count. This series is present when Flashblocks are enabled.
panels.title: Flashblocks Peers

panels.description: Logical/estimated World Chain storage: MDBX tables and freelist, static files, RocksDB tables, and RocksDB WAL. RocksDB table_size already includes SST and memtable data.

targets.expr: ((sum(reth_db_table_size{job="$worldchain_job"})) or vector(0)) + ((sum(reth_db_freelist{job="$worldchain_job"} * reth_db_page_size{job="$worldchain_job"})) or vector(0)) + ((sum(reth_static_files_segment_size{job="$worldchain_job"})) or vector(0)) + ((sum(reth_rocksdb_table_size{job="$worldchain_job"})) or vector(0)) + ((sum(reth_rocksdb_wal_size{job="$worldchain_job"})) or vector(0))

panels.title: Total Storage

panels.description: Execution-layer checkpoints and chain heads are shown beside OP Node derivation heads. Peering is split because World Chain, OP Node, and Flashblocks use distinct P2P networks.
panels.title: Synchronization & Peering

panels.description: Execution-layer canonical, safe, and finalized block heights.
panels.title: World Chain Heads

panels.description: Consensus/derivation heads reported by OP Node 1.19.2.
panels.title: OP Node L2 Heads

panels.description: Completion ratio for each execution pipeline stage. A value of 100% means that stage has processed all currently scheduled entities.
panels.title: World Chain Sync Status by Stage

panels.description: Wall-clock age of OP Node's L2 heads. Safe/finalized ages naturally trail unsafe.
panels.title: OP Node Head Age

panels.description: Rollup P2P bandwidth by direction. Flashblocks bandwidth is shown in its dedicated section.
panels.title: OP Node P2P Bandwidth

panels.description: Engine API latency, gas, throughput, and validation phases. Standard newPayload paths remain useful when Flashblocks are enabled; Flashblock-specific execution and BAL-aware comparisons follow in a dedicated section.
panels.title: Engine & Execution Performance

panels.description: Gas/s measured three ways: full newPayload response; EVM-only execution; and latest gas divided by EVM execution plus state-root time.
panels.title: Gas Throughput

panels.description: newPayload gas/s split into <5M, 5–10M, 10–20M, 20–30M, 30–40M, and >40M gas buckets.
panels.title: Gas-Bucketed newPayload Throughput

panels.description: Cache effectiveness is separated by engine/builder source when available. Precompile cache metrics are counters labeled by precompile address.
panels.title: Execution & Precompile Caches

panels.description: Rate-based hit ratio by precompile address.
panels.title: Precompile Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Storage is split across MDBX, RocksDB, and static files in World Chain 2.4.0. RocksDB table_size includes SST and memtable estimates; WAL is displayed separately to prevent double-counting.
panels.title: Storage

panels.description: RocksDB-backed history and transaction index tables.
panels.title: RocksDB by Table

panels.description: SST and memtable are components of table_size and must not be added to table_size again.
panels.title: RocksDB Physical Layout

panels.description: 15-minute linear-regression growth rate. Negative values can occur after pruning, compaction, or WAL rotation.
panels.title: Storage Growth

panels.description: MDBX is transactional; RocksDB is operation/batch oriented. The panels therefore show transaction lifecycle phases for MDBX and per-operation latency/rate plus compaction pressure for RocksDB.
panels.title: Database I/O

panels.description: Get, put, delete, and batch-write latency by RocksDB table. RocksDB has no MDBX-style transaction-open lifecycle.
panels.title: RocksDB Operation Latency

panels.description: Pruner runtime, segment cost, and progress. Storage growth can fall during active pruning or RocksDB compaction.
panels.title: Pruning

panels.description: World Chain 2.4.0 Flashblocks validator and P2P metrics, plus EIP-7928 Block-Level Access List (BAL) metrics. BAL comparisons use the access_list label emitted by flashblocks.validate.
panels.title: Flashblocks & BALs

panels.description: Distribution-level estimate: p50 gas divided by p50 duration. It is not an event-correlated rate because World Chain 2.4.0 exports gas and duration as separate histograms.
panels.title: Flashblock Gas Throughput (p50 estimate)

panels.description: End-to-end flashblock validator span, split by whether an access list was present. This custom metric records milliseconds.
panels.title: BAL vs Non-BAL Flashblock Validation

panels.description: Share of validated Flashblocks that carried a BAL. World Chain 2.4.0 does not yet emit BAL size/change counters, so the dashboard uses the actively emitted access_list label rather than showing dormant upstream series.
panels.title: BAL Flashblock Share

panels.description: Completed Flashblock validations per second, split by BAL presence.
panels.title: BAL Validation Rate

panels.description: Process-level CPU, memory, file descriptors, runtime activity, and high-signal error/backpressure indicators. Host-wide disk/CPU saturation requires a host exporter and is not inferred from process metrics.
panels.title: Resources & Operational Health

panels.description: Process CPU can exceed 100% when multiple cores are used.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description: Kept as a compact load indicator because RPC demand can explain CPU, memory, and database pressure.
panels.title: RPC Throughput
